Methods and results for the Chapter 4 population structure analysis. Upstream Gadi steps (PLINK 2, ADMIXTURE, vcftools) are documented but not rerun; their saved outputs are read here. Replaces `pop_gen.R` (archived unchanged in `snapshot/local/genomic_data/pop_gen/`).

## 1. Setup and inputs

```{r setup}
library(SNPRelate)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(plotly)
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

set.seed(43)  # arbitrary; only matters for permutation tests added later

data_dir <- Sys.getenv("POPGEN_DATA",
  unset = "C:/Users/evane/OneDrive/Desktop/Masters Dissertation/genomic_data/pop_gen")
out_dir <- "output"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

species_colors <- c(
  "Eucalyptus pauciflora subsp. niphophila" = "#56B4E9",
  "Eucalyptus pauciflora subsp. pauciflora" = "#E69F00",
  "Eucalyptus stellulata"                   = "#CC79A7"
)
taxa <- names(species_colors)

# plink2's VCF export doubles sample IDs (ID_ID); strip for display only
undouble <- function(x) sub("^(.*)_\\1$", "\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
```

| File in `data_dir` | Source |
|---|---|
| `snowgums_200k_pruned.vcf.gz` | LD-pruned variants (below) |
| `snowgums_200k_stride.vcf.gz` | Stride-thinned variants (`stride_sample.sh`) |
| `snowgums_clean_pruned.{bed,bim,fam}`, `.K1-7.log`, `.1-7.Q` | ADMIXTURE 1.4.0 (section 5) |
| `het_*.het`, `freq_*.afreq` | PLINK 2 (section 6) |
| `pairwise_fst_results.fst.summary` | PLINK 2 (section 7) |
| `fst_*_50kb.windowed.weir.fst` | vcftools (section 8) |
| `chr6_region_pca.eigenvec`, `chr6_region_het.het` | PLINK 2 (section 9) |
| `pauci_stellulata_1minusIBS.mdist(.id)` | PLINK, 382 samples (section 11) |

**LD pruning** (PLINK 2, Gadi, 2 Sep 2026): 20,450,435 variants after removing 87 with duplicated IDs; 197,879 retained.

```
plink2 --bfile snowgum_filtered --rm-dup force-first \
  --set-all-var-ids @:#:$r:$a --new-id-max-allele-len 97 \
  --indep-pairwise 100kb 1 0.05 --out pruned_snps
```

Sample metadata are read from the Google Sheet (source of truth).

```{r metadata}
euc_meta <- read_csv(
  "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QI4KE4M7i8ST6mLNoG8rkkfkUio_3AGQRQY6PQ3Sg24/export?gid=4473427&format=csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(fastq_sample_name = paste(fastq_sample_name, fastq_sample_name, sep = "_"))
```

```{r gds}
pruned_gds_path <- file.path(data_dir, "snowgums_200k_pruned.gds")
if (!file.exists(pruned_gds_path)) {
  snpgdsVCF2GDS(file.path(data_dir, "snowgums_200k_pruned.vcf.gz"), pruned_gds_path, verbose = FALSE)
}
pruned_gds <- snpgdsOpen(pruned_gds_path)
pruned_info <- snpgdsSummary(pruned_gds, show = FALSE)

initial_good_samples <- pruned_info$sample.id[pruned_info$sample.id %in% euc_meta$fastq_sample_name]
meta <- euc_meta[match(initial_good_samples, euc_meta$fastq_sample_name), ] %>%
  mutate(species_clean = species %>% str_replace("X.*", "") %>% str_replace(" x .*", ""))
taxon_of <- setNames(meta$species_clean, meta$fastq_sample_name)

cat("SNPs:", length(pruned_info$snp.id), "| samples:", length(initial_good_samples), "(expected 197,879 and 390)\n")
```

## 2. Kinship

KING-robust kinship (Manichaikul et al. 2010; `snpgdsIBDKING`) on the 197,879 LD-pruned SNPs. Pairs above 0.177 (geometric mean of the first-degree and second-degree expectations, 0.25 and 0.125) were treated as relatives, and the sample with the higher missingness in each pair was excluded.

```{r kinship, cache=TRUE}
king <- snpgdsIBDKING(pruned_gds, sample.id = initial_good_samples, autosome.only = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
kinship_mat <- king$kinship
rownames(kinship_mat) <- colnames(kinship_mat) <- king$sample.id

close_relatives <- kinship_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample_1, names_to = "sample_2", values_to = "kinship") %>%
  filter(sample_1 < sample_2, kinship > 0.177) %>%
  arrange(desc(kinship))
write_csv(close_relatives, file.path(out_dir, "king_close_relative_pairs.csv"))

missrate <- snpgdsSampMissRate(pruned_gds, sample.id = initial_good_samples)
names(missrate) <- initial_good_samples

related_exclusions <- close_relatives %>%
  mutate(exclude = if_else(missrate[sample_1] >= missrate[sample_2], sample_1, sample_2)) %>%
  pull(exclude) %>% unique()

n_before_kinship <- length(initial_good_samples)
initial_good_samples <- setdiff(initial_good_samples, related_exclusions)
meta <- meta %>% filter(!fastq_sample_name %in% related_exclusions)
```

```{r kinship-table}
close_relatives %>%
  mutate(across(c(sample_1, sample_2), undouble), kinship = round(kinship, 3)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pairs above the relatedness threshold")
cat("Excluded:", paste(undouble(related_exclusions), collapse = ", "),
    "| samples:", n_before_kinship, "->", length(initial_good_samples), "\n")
```

```{r fig-kinship}
#| fig-cap: "Pairwise kinship (KING-robust), all samples before exclusions. Ordered by taxon (strip: niphophila, pauciflora, stellulata), then by hierarchical clustering within taxon. Bright off-diagonal cells are close relatives."
ord_ids <- unlist(lapply(split(names(taxon_of), taxon_of)[names(species_colors)], function(ids) {
  ids <- intersect(ids, rownames(kinship_mat))
  if (length(ids) < 3) return(ids)
  ids[hclust(as.dist(0.5 - kinship_mat[ids, ids]), method = "average")$order]
}), use.names = FALSE)

kin_ord <- kinship_mat[ord_ids, ord_ids]
diag(kin_ord) <- NA
heat_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(kin_ord)) %>% setNames(c("row", "col", "kinship"))

heat <- ggplot(heat_df, aes(col, row, fill = kinship)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Kinship", na.value = "white") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), limits = rev) +
  theme_void()

strip <- ggplot(tibble(id = factor(ord_ids, levels = ord_ids), taxon = taxon_of[ord_ids]),
                aes(id, 1, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_void() + theme(legend.position = "none")

strip / heat + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 30))
```

## 3. Principal component analysis

`snpgdsPCA` on the LD-pruned panel, all sequence classes included (`autosome.only = FALSE`). The 76 *E. stellulata* samples are the outgroup. Outliers are removed iteratively: each round runs PCA, drops samples meeting that round's filter, and reruns. Here one round was used (`PC01 < -0.2`).

```{r pca, cache=TRUE}
pca_to_df <- function(pca) {
  df <- as.data.frame(pca$eigenvect)
  colnames(df) <- sprintf("PC%02d", seq_len(ncol(df)))
  mutate(df, sample_id = as.character(pca$sample.id))
}

run_iterative_pca_cleanup <- function(gds, samples, filters) {
  removed <- tibble(sample_id = character(), round = integer(), filter = character())
  for (i in seq_along(filters)) {
    pca <- snpgdsPCA(gds, sample.id = samples, autosome.only = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
    out <- pca$sample.id[eval(parse(text = filters[i]), envir = pca_to_df(pca))]
    removed <- bind_rows(removed, tibble(sample_id = out, round = i, filter = filters[i]))
    samples <- setdiff(samples, out)
  }
  pca <- snpgdsPCA(gds, sample.id = samples, autosome.only = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  list(pca = pca, df = pca_to_df(pca), removed = removed)
}

pca_results <- run_iterative_pca_cleanup(pruned_gds, initial_good_samples, "PC01 < -0.2")

pca_data <- pca_results$df %>%
  left_join(meta, by = join_by(sample_id == fastq_sample_name)) %>%
  mutate(short_id = undouble(sample_id))

writeLines(pca_results$pca$sample.id, file.path(out_dir, "final_pca_samples.txt"))
```

```{r pca-counts}
cat("Removed:", paste(undouble(pca_results$removed$sample_id), collapse = ", "),
    "| samples:", nrow(pca_data), "(thesis: four removed)\n")
```

Choose the PC for each axis from the dropdowns, click a legend entry to hide a taxon (double-click to isolate it), and hover for sample IDs. Thesis Fig. 7a is PC1 vs PC2 and Fig. 7b is PC1 vs PC3.

```{r fig-pca}
# One or two panels; the dropdowns and the legend act on all panels
interactive_pca <- function(dfs, pcas, titles = NULL, n_pc = 10) {
  n <- length(dfs)
  sfx <- c("", "2")[seq_len(n)]
  dom <- if (n == 1) list(c(0, 1)) else list(c(0, 0.47), c(0.53, 1))
  pcs <- sprintf("PC%02d", seq_len(n_pc))
  pc_lab <- lapply(pcas, function(p) sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", pcs, p$varprop[seq_len(n_pc)] * 100))
  by_taxon <- lapply(dfs, function(d) split(d, factor(d$species_clean, levels = taxa)))

  p <- plot_ly()
  for (k in seq_len(n)) for (tx in taxa) {
    d <- by_taxon[[k]][[tx]]
    p <- add_trace(p, x = d$PC01, y = d$PC02, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
                   xaxis = paste0("x", sfx[k]), yaxis = paste0("y", sfx[k]),
                   name = tx, legendgroup = tx, showlegend = (k == 1),
                   text = d$short_id, hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>%{x:.3f}, %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>",
                   marker = list(color = species_colors[[tx]], size = 8, opacity = 0.85))
  }

  axis_menu <- function(axis, active, x_pos) {
    list(type = "dropdown", direction = "down", active = active - 1,
         x = x_pos, y = 1.12, xanchor = "left", yanchor = "top",
         buttons = lapply(seq_along(pcs), function(i) {
           vals <- unlist(lapply(by_taxon, function(bt) lapply(bt, function(d) d[[pcs[i]]])), recursive = FALSE)
           axis_titles <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(n), function(k) pc_lab[[k]][i]),
                                   paste0(axis, "axis", sfx, ".title.text"))
           list(method = "update", label = pcs[i],
                args = list(setNames(list(unname(vals)), axis), axis_titles))
         }))
  }

  ann <- list(list(text = "x", x = 0,    y = 1.085, xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE),
              list(text = "y", x = 0.26, y = 1.085, xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE))
  if (!is.null(titles)) for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    ann[[length(ann) + 1]] <- list(text = paste0("<b>", titles[k], "</b>"), x = mean(dom[[k]]), y = 1,
                                   xref = "paper", yref = "paper", showarrow = FALSE, yanchor = "bottom")
  }

  lay <- list(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15), margin = list(t = 90),
              updatemenus = list(axis_menu("x", 1, 0.04), axis_menu("y", 2, 0.30)),
              annotations = ann)
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    lay[[paste0("xaxis", sfx[k])]] <- list(domain = dom[[k]], anchor = paste0("y", sfx[k]),
                                           title = list(text = pc_lab[[k]][1]), zeroline = FALSE)
    lay[[paste0("yaxis", sfx[k])]] <- list(domain = c(0, 1), anchor = paste0("x", sfx[k]),
                                           title = list(text = pc_lab[[k]][2]), zeroline = FALSE)
  }
  do.call(layout, c(list(p), lay))
}

interactive_pca(list(pca_data), list(pca_results$pca))
```

### Distance outlier

One further sample (MON0667) was excluded by name for an anomalously high mean distance to all other samples; the PCA above includes it. Distance is 1 minus identity-by-state (`snpgdsIBS`) on the LD-pruned panel.

```{r distance-outlier}
technical_outlier_exclusions <- "MON0667_MON0667"

ibs <- snpgdsIBS(pruned_gds, sample.id = pca_results$pca$sample.id, autosome.only = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
mean_dist <- tibble(sample_id = ibs$sample.id,
                    mean_dist = rowSums(1 - ibs$ibs) / (nrow(ibs$ibs) - 1)) %>%
  mutate(taxon = taxon_of[sample_id])

out_row <- filter(mean_dist, sample_id == technical_outlier_exclusions)
peers <- filter(mean_dist, taxon == out_row$taxon, sample_id != technical_outlier_exclusions)

tibble(Sample = undouble(out_row$sample_id), Taxon = out_row$taxon,
       `Mean distance` = out_row$mean_dist,
       `Taxon mean (others)` = mean(peers$mean_dist),
       `Taxon SD (others)` = sd(peers$mean_dist),
       `z score` = (out_row$mean_dist - mean(peers$mean_dist)) / sd(peers$mean_dist)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
  kable()

ggplot(mean_dist, aes(mean_dist, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = out_row$mean_dist, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = out_row$mean_dist, y = Inf, label = "MON0667", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 2, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors) +
  labs(x = "Mean 1 - IBS to all other samples", y = "Samples", fill = "Taxa") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

clean_sample_ids <- setdiff(pca_data$sample_id, technical_outlier_exclusions)
cat("Analysis set:", length(clean_sample_ids), "samples (thesis: 382 = 260 + 46 + 76)\n")
```

## 4. Sensitivity: LD-pruned versus stride-thinned panel

PCA used the LD-pruned panel because it is the principled choice (independent SNPs). LD pruning also removes the high-LD sites an inversion creates, so it may weaken inversion-linked structure. The same cleanup and PCA are run here on the stride-thinned panel (every n-th SNP, no LD criterion) from the same post-kinship samples, and the removed individuals are compared.

PC signs are arbitrary between runs, so the threshold applies to this run's orientation. Add a filter after inspecting each round.

```{r stride-pca, cache=TRUE}
stride_vcf <- file.path(data_dir, "snowgums_200k_stride.vcf.gz")
stride_path <- file.path(data_dir, "snowgums_200k_stride.gds")
if (!file.exists(stride_path)) snpgdsVCF2GDS(stride_vcf, stride_path, verbose = FALSE)
stride_gds <- snpgdsOpen(stride_path)
stride_info <- snpgdsSummary(stride_gds, show = FALSE)

stride_filters <- c("PC02 > 0.25", "PC01 < -0.2", "PC02 > 0.2")
stride_results <- run_iterative_pca_cleanup(
  stride_gds, intersect(initial_good_samples, stride_info$sample.id), stride_filters)
stride_df <- stride_results$df %>%
  left_join(meta, by = join_by(sample_id == fastq_sample_name)) %>%
  mutate(short_id = undouble(sample_id))
snpgdsClose(stride_gds)
```

```{r stride-tables}
tibble(
  Panel = c("LD-pruned", "Stride-thinned"),
  SNPs = c(length(pruned_info$snp.id), length(stride_info$snp.id)),
  Samples = c(nrow(pca_data), nrow(stride_df)),
  `PC1 (%)` = round(c(pca_results$pca$varprop[1], stride_results$pca$varprop[1]) * 100, 2),
  `PC2 (%)` = round(c(pca_results$pca$varprop[2], stride_results$pca$varprop[2]) * 100, 2),
  `PC3 (%)` = round(c(pca_results$pca$varprop[3], stride_results$pca$varprop[3]) * 100, 2)
) %>% kable(caption = "Final PCA on each panel")

full_join(
  select(pca_results$removed, sample_id, `LD-pruned round` = round),
  select(stride_results$removed, sample_id, `Stride round` = round), by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(Taxon = taxon_of[sample_id], Sample = undouble(sample_id)) %>%
  select(Sample, Taxon, `LD-pruned round`, `Stride round`) %>%
  arrange(Taxon, Sample) %>%
  kable(caption = "Samples removed by iterative cleanup (blank: not removed on that panel)")
```

The dropdowns set the axes of both panels, and the legend toggles taxa in both.

```{r fig-stride}
interactive_pca(list(pca_data, stride_df), list(pca_results$pca, stride_results$pca),
                titles = c("LD-pruned", "Stride-thinned"))
```

## 5. ADMIXTURE (to convert)

```
admixture --cv=5 -s 43 snowgums_clean_pruned.bed K    # K = 1 to 7; command reconstructed from the logs
```

382 samples, 197,879 SNPs, one run per K. CV error: K1 0.44437, K2 0.43577, K3 0.43549, K4 0.43847, K5 0.44555, K6 0.45065, K7 0.45799. Reads `.K*.log` and `.{2,3}.Q`. Output: Figs. 8 and 9.

## 6. Heterozygosity (to convert)

```
plink2 --allow-extra-chr --bfile snowgum_filtered --keep keep_<taxon>.txt --rm-dup force-first --freq --out freq_<taxon>
plink2 --allow-extra-chr --bfile snowgum_filtered --keep keep_<taxon>.txt --rm-dup force-first --het --read-freq freq_<taxon>.afreq --out het_<taxon>
```

Used as written for *pauciflora* and *stellulata* (8 Oct). The *niphophila* file was rerun on 17 Nov as `--het small-sample` without `--allow-extra-chr` or `--rm-dup`, and PLINK ignored `--read-freq`. Reproduce Table 1 from these files before reporting it.

## 7. Genome-wide Fst (to convert)

```
plink2 --allow-extra-chr --bfile snowgum_filtered --keep admixture_keep_samples_fixed.txt \
  --pheno taxa_pheno_fixed.txt --pheno-name Taxon --fst Taxon method=wc --out pairwise_fst_results
```

Weir and Cockerham, 382 samples, three taxa. Output: Fig. 10.

## 8. Windowed Fst (to convert)

vcftools, 50 kb windows (`windowed_fst.sh`). Reads the three `.windowed.weir.fst` files. Output: Figs. 11 and 12, and the chromosome 6 block (CM074670.1, about 38 to 48.5 Mb) against background. The thesis text cites Figs. 12 and 13 for these; the captions number them 11 and 12.

## 9. Local PCA, chromosome 6 (to convert)

```
plink2 --allow-extra-chr --bfile chr6_region_pauci_niph --pca 10 --out chr6_region_pca
plink2 --allow-extra-chr --bfile chr6_region_pauci_niph --het --out chr6_region_het
```

306 samples, 515,243 variants. The command that built `chr6_region_pauci_niph` is not yet located. Output: Fig. 13, plus a saved sample-by-cluster (putative karyotype) table.

## 10. Latent factors (to convert)

Scree plot of the *pauciflora*-only PCA supporting K = 9 for LFMM. Output: Fig. 14 (not made by the original script).

## 11. Isolation by distance (to convert)

Reads `pauci_stellulata_1minusIBS.mdist(.id)` (382 samples, Gadi version; command in the `.log`). Mantel tests with permutations for Appendix 3; set the seed first.

## 12. Decisions and quirks

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| PCA panel | LD-pruned, chosen on principle, not from comparing outputs; compared in section 4. |
| Sample IDs | plink2 VCF export doubles IDs (`ID_ID`); metadata are matched to that format. |
| MON0667 | Excluded by name after the PCA; already absent from the Gadi distance matrix. |
| Distance matrix | Laptop copy had 383 samples (included MON0667); the 382-sample Gadi copy is canonical. Old file in `old/`. |
| Heterozygosity | *niphophila* run differs from the others (section 6). |
| ADMIXTURE | One run per K, seed 43; command reconstructed. |
| Mantel tests | Original script set no seed. |
| R packages | Not recorded originally; see session information. |

## Notes for the paper (not acted on)

**Planned**

- More *niphophila* data (currently n = 49, two sky islands).
- dxy (a workaround exists that Kevin Murray knows about).
- All other subspecies, when available.
- Focus on chromosome 6, possibly with a reference assembly per subspecies; long-read sequencing is under way, at least for *niphophila* and *pauciflora*.
- A third subspecies would span the sequencing spectrum: *pauciflora* mostly short read, *niphophila* split, others almost entirely long read.

**Observations**

- dxy needs per-site denominators (callable invariant sites); the current VCF is variant-only with MAC > 10, so dxy from it is biased. Compute it between karyotype classes as well as between subspecies.
- Choose long-read individuals as homozygotes of each local-PCA cluster, with haplotype-resolved assemblies; polarize the arrangement with *E. regnans* and *E. stellulata*.
- Platform is confounded with taxon in the planned design, and mixed-platform PCA can cluster by platform. Sequencing a few *niphophila* individuals on both platforms would measure platform error and reference bias.
- ADMIXTURE replicates (several seeds per K) would test whether K = 3 is stable and whether the K = 4 northern split is reproducible.
- Save the chromosome 6 karyotype table as a durable output.
